'''Peter Barker''' (born 1967) is an Australian-born British physicist.

Barker obtained his PhD in Physics in 1996 from the [[University of Queensland]] under the supervision of [[Halina Rubinsztein-Dunlop]].<ref>{{Cite thesis |last=Barker |first=Peter F. |title=The development of laser based diagnostic techniques for application to supersonic and hypersonic flows |date=1996-01-01 |degree=PhD |publisher=University of Queensland |url=https://espace.library.uq.edu.au/view/UQ:321545 |doi=10.14264/321545 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240730145129/https://espace.library.uq.edu.au/view/UQ:321545 |archive-date=2024-07-30|url-access=subscription }}</ref>

From 1997 to 2000, he was a postdoctoral fellow and lecturer at [[Princeton University]] in the US. From 2001 to 2006, he was a lecturer at [[Heriot-Watt University]] in Edinburgh in the UK. He held an [[EPSRC]] Research Fellowship from 2005–2010. In 2006, he moved to [[University College London]] as Reader and became a Professor in 2007.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.ucl.ac.uk/physics-astronomy/people/professor-peter-barker |title=Professor Peter Barker |last=UCL |date=2018-04-25 |website=UCL Department of Physics and Astronomy |language=en |access-date=2018-12-06}}</ref>

He was the head of the [[Atomic physics|Atomic]], [[Molecular]], [[Optical]] and [[Positron]] [[Physics]] group in the Department of Physics and Astronomy at [[University College London]] (UCL). Since 2005, his research has concentrated on the cooling, manipulation and transport of atoms, molecules and [[nanoparticles]] in [[optical tweezers]].<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Anders|first1=J.|last2=Barker|first2=P.|last3=Deesuwan|first3=T.|last4=Millen|first4=J.|date=June 2014|title=Nanoscale temperature measurements using non-equilibrium Brownian dynamics of a levitated nanosphere|journal=Nature Nanotechnology|language=en|volume=9|issue=6|pages=425–429|doi=10.1038/nnano.2014.82|pmid=24793558|issn=1748-3395|arxiv=1309.3990|bibcode=2014NatNa...9..425M }}</ref> In 2017, he began to explore experimental approaches to create a micron-sized fridge using optical refrigeration of a submicrometre crystal suspended in optical and [[ion traps]].<ref name=":0">{{Cite journal|last1=Barker|first1=P. F.|last2=Rahman|first2=A. T. M. Anishur|date=October 2017|title=Laser refrigeration, alignment and rotation of levitated Yb 3+ :YLF nanocrystals|journal=Nature Photonics|language=en|volume=11|issue=10|pages=634–638|doi=10.1038/s41566-017-0005-3|issn=1749-4893|url=http://discovery.ucl.ac.uk/10064662/1/refriglev2ndRevisionpb.pdf}}</ref>
